accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are taught with bounded claims: persistence needs recovery, models overlap, specialized queries have different semantics, and CAP applies during partitions. No false guarantee. Supplemental primary documentation fills gaps in broad slide links.

evidence.quote: An isolated reader cannot learn a completed write from an unreachable copy. Returning old data sacrifices consistency; waiting indefinitely or refusing the affected operation sacrifices availability.

mechanisms.reason: The learner can trace layout to query/update work, duplication to coordinated changes, index maintenance to write costs, and an unreachable completed write to the CAP conflict. The record and specialized-query diagrams express these access patterns correctly rather than rank products.

evidence.quote: Keeping shared facts in one place reduces duplicate updates but can require joins at read time. Embedding copies can simplify reads while adding updates to coordinate. A new access pattern may need another layout or index.

In Cassandra-style layouts, a partition key groups records for targeted access. Design that grouping around known queries. Poor keys can overload a partition; a new query may need a new table. This data partition is distinct from a network partition, which is a communication failure.

coherence.reason: Database role and requirements precede record models, specialized access and overlapping capabilities; costs and partition behavior then support the final choice method. All eight card objectives connect, without requiring an artificial recurring scenario.

evidence.quote: Connect each requirement to a data layout or capability, then name its write, storage, coordination or operating cost. If copies are distributed, explain behavior when they cannot communicate.

decisions.reason: The choice method explicitly combines queries, correctness, recovery and operating ability with measurable costs. It explains when existing capabilities suffice, when another store may help, and which measurements or changed requirements reverse a choice.

evidence.quote: Keeping these tasks together can reduce the number of systems to run. A separate service can still make sense when workload needs or operating limits justify it. Measure those needs instead of assuming one store must do everything.
Measure representative queries and updates. Changed access patterns, traffic or recovery requirements can change the choice; popularity and product names are not substitutes for this reasoning.

clarity.reason: Rows, documents, keys, partition keys, graph edges, embeddings, indexes and both CAP meanings are defined before use. Diagrams distinguish the same record layouts and query types; data partition versus network partition is explicit. Detail matches introductory scope.

evidence.quote: An embedding represents an item as a list of numbers. Similarity search finds nearby vectors under a chosen measure; it can support retrieval by meaning. Approximate search trades some result accuracy for speed. Similarity does not prove exact equality or factual correctness.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria are entailed by slides 1, 2 and 8 and the actual learner quotes: managed persistence and operations, application coupling, configured recovery, record/query/update discovery, cross-change rules and growth/latency/operations, and category limits. Finding/filtering/combining and main-query identification supply the required access-pattern reasoning.

All six criteria are supported by slides 3–4 and their diagrams: rows/columns/joins, nested reads versus duplicate updates, known-key access limits, query-oriented partition grouping distinct from network failure, edge traversal, and numeric similarity without equality/truth. The learner correctly limits unsupported algorithm details.

All six criteria are supported across slides 2 and 4–6: spatial/vector overlap, actual capability and workload checks rather than equal guarantees, extra-store synchronization/operations, index space and writes, duplicate-update coordination, and distributed communication/partial failure costs. Possible disagreement between copies follows from the taught need to coordinate updates; no prior knowledge is needed.

All six criteria are explicitly taught in slides 5, 7 and 8 and correctly reconstructed by the learner: copies and communication loss, current-copy/response meanings and impossibility, affected-operation/configuration scope, requirements-first choice, accepted cost and recovery behavior, and representative measurement/reconsideration without vendor or multiple-store requirements.

sourceChecks.claim: Opened relational concepts; persistence/recovery scope additionally checked against https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/backup.html. The source link alone is introductory, not a complete recovery reference.

Opened JSON documentation, confirming relational JSON support. Document transactions verified at https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions/ with configured concerns; requirements-first choices are synthesis, not claimed product benchmarks.

Opened MongoDB modeling: nested records and accessed-together embedding. Joins checked at https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-join.html; direct key/value retrieval at https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/strings/. Diagram representations are consistent with these models.

Opened Cassandra logical modeling: table-per-query and partition-key/query fit. Graph traversal independently checked at https://neo4j.com/docs/getting-started/appendix/graphdb-concepts/; vectors and approximate speed/recall trade-off at https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector. Numeric distance alone entails neither semantic truth nor equality.

Opened PostGIS documentation landing page and actual spatial query chapter https://postgis.net/docs/manual-3.6/using_postgis_query.html for containment, spatial joins and indexes. PostgreSQL vector extension checked at https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector. No comparative performance is asserted.

Opened index introduction: avoids full scan for suitable predicates and adds maintenance overhead. Duplication/access costs supported by MongoDB modeling and Cassandra query-driven layouts; partition communication costs checked against linked FoundationDB CAP explanation.

Opened full CAP explanation, including distinction between formal availability at all non-failing nodes and ordinary service uptime. Lesson correctly bounds the conflict to affected operations during communication failure and avoids universal SQL/NoSQL classification.

Opened concepts page; final requirements/capability/cost method is defensible synthesis of inspected modeling, index and failure sources. It makes no unverified deployment measurement or vendor guarantee.
